message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it might be a STEMI, right?
reply:
**I wouldn’t call this a definite STEMI from the image, but it needs clinical assessment if it’s a current ECG.**

I see sinus rhythm, prominent anterior T waves with some ST elevation in V2–V3, and very high QRS voltages—deep S waves in V1–V3 and tall R waves in V4–V6. That suggests **left ventricular hypertrophy with associated repolarization changes**, which can mimic STEMI. I don’t see convincing reciprocal ST depression.

However, **this ECG alone cannot rule out an acute coronary blockage**. Symptoms, comparison with an old ECG, repeat ECGs, and troponin testing matter; LV hypertrophy also complicates standard STEMI criteria. [ESC guidelines](https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/44/38/3720/7243210)

If there’s current chest discomfort, breathlessness, sweating, or faintness, call emergency services now and don’t drive yourself.

What prompted the ECG, how old is the patient, and are they having symptoms now?
